note: E1: caseworker with four tools and a 10-step loop, no verifier. Same model, same policy, same dossier as the baseline.

cases.title: Cancelled short-notice flight, crew shortage
cases.rationale: Flight MR414 was cancelled (S2.1(a)), a carrier-controlled disruption caused by crew duty hours exhaustion (S3.2(b)). Cancellation notified 3 March for 6 March departure—less than 7 days notice (S4.2)—entitling full 100% compensation. Distance 2,090 km falls in Band B (S5.1), yielding 420 units. No alternative routing was offered, so S4.4 exemption does not apply. Evidence is sufficient per S8.1(a), (b), and (e). Duty of care is owed per S6.1, but no receipts on file; if claimed, must provide itemised receipts per S6.4.

cases.title: Weather cancellation with overnight duty of care
cases.rationale: Flight NW220 was cancelled (S2.1(a)) due to extraordinary weather—OSL below operating minima (S3.3(a))—so no Part 5 compensation is payable per S3.1. However, S6.1 requires duty of care reimbursement regardless of cause. The carrier's rejection incorrectly states it is 'unable to reimburse your expenses' and is validly challengeable under S9.1(e) for being silent on duty of care. Passenger's itemised receipts (D4) total 240 units—hotel 190, meals 50—and fall within the 300-unit duty-of-care cap (S6.3).

cases.title: Unforeseen technical fault, six-hour delay, long haul
cases.rationale: Insufficient evidence to confirm scope without claim filing date per S1.2(c). If filed within 18 months of scheduled departure 02 Sep 2026, passenger qualifies under S2.1(b): 6h 06m delay at final destination NBO. Cause is carrier-controlled S3.2(a): LP's line maintenance detected the bleed air valve fault during pre-departure checks (D4), with no manufacturer or regulator directive per S3.4. Compensation would be 750 units (Band C, 6,635 km distance, no taper at ≥5h delay per S5.4). Request evidence of claim filing date to proceed.

cases.title: Missed connection on one booking, tapered delay
cases.rationale: Passenger held a confirmed booking on both segments under single reference MT5590 (D1). MT119 delayed 2h 35m due to MT ground-handling shortfall at MAD (D3, S3.2 carrier-controlled), causing missed connection at DOH. Final arrival 4h 10m late (D4), qualifying under S2.1(b) and S2.3. Distance 17,680 km is Band C (750 units, S5.1). Delay falls in 3h 30m–5h band, triggering S5.4 tapering to 50%: 750 × 0.5 = 375 units. No Part 4 notice reduction applies to delays (S4.6). Claim merits submission to carrier.

cases.title: Missed connection across two separate bookings
cases.rationale: The passenger held two independently purchased bookings with no interline agreement. Under S2.3, separate booking references are treated as separate journeys, so the final destination of the first journey is FRA (the connecting airport), not IST. JJ88 arrived at FRA 55 minutes late (D3, D4), falling short of the 3 hour 30 minute threshold required by S2.1(b). The claim is in scope but does not qualify for compensation.

cases.title: Twelve days notice with a compliant re-routing offer
cases.rationale: The flight was cancelled on 8 June 11:40 for 20 June departure, giving 11 days 21 hours' notice—within S4.2's 7–20 day band. However, S4.3 exempts from compensation any cancellation where re-routing is offered departing no more than 2 hours before and arriving less than 4 hours after the original. Vantage offered VN517 departing at 08:00 (1 hour before VN515's 09:00) and arriving 16:00 (3 hours 30 minutes after VN515's 12:30). The exemption applies. No compensation is payable.

cases.title: Fourteen days notice, non-compliant re-route, exact band boundary
cases.rationale: Flight ZR260 was cancelled (S2.1(a)), caused by crew rostering system failure, a carrier-controlled cause under S3.2(c). Cancellation notification sent 17 Sep 2026, scheduled departure 01 Oct 2026, equals 14 days' notice, placing the claim in the 7–20 day band (S4.2: 50% compensation). Re-routing exemption S4.3 does not apply: offered flight departs 18:20 (1h35m after 16:45, outside the required 2-hour prior window) and arrives 01:35 next day (5h20m after original 20:15, exceeding the 4-hour limit). Distance exactly 1,200 km: Band A applies per S5.3 (180 units). Final compensation: 180 × 0.5 = 90 units. Evidence sufficient: booking (D1), cancellation notice with timestamp (D2), boarding pass for replacement (D3), operational cause confirmed (D4).

cases.title: Cancellation with twenty-five days notice
cases.rationale: The booking is confirmed (S1.2(a,b)) and the disruption qualifies under S2.1(a). Notification was sent 16 Nov 2026; departure scheduled 12 Dec 2026—26 days notice. Under S4.2, notice of 21 days or more attracts zero Part 5 compensation. Duty of care is owed (S6.1) regardless of cause, but S6.4 requires itemised receipts to substantiate any claim.

cases.title: Delay claim with no arrival-time evidence
cases.rationale: Booking is confirmed (D1, S1.2(a)), passenger boarded (D2, S1.2(b)), and claim is timely (about 3 months, well under S1.2(c)'s 18-month limit). Operational record shows a carrier-controlled cause: unscheduled hydraulic pump replacement (D3, S3.2(a)). However, D3 states the arrival record is not attached. Per S8.1(c), evidence of actual arrival time at the final destination is mandatory to determine if S2.1(b) (3h30m or more late) applies. The passenger's estimate of 'about four or five hours' is not documentary proof. Cannot proceed without the actual arrival timestamp from the carrier's operational records.

cases.title: Cancellation with no notification timestamp
cases.rationale: The booking was confirmed (D1) and the flight was cancelled due to crew sickness (D2, S3.2(b)), a carrier-controlled cause. The claim is in scope and qualifies under S2.1(a). However, S8.1(e) requires the carrier's cancellation notification with timestamp to determine the advance notice period and calculate compensation under the Part 4 ladder. This document is not in the record—D2 states the passenger notification dispatch log was not included. The passenger's recollection in D3 ('6th or 7th') cannot substitute per the directive to distrust passenger claims without corroborating evidence.

cases.title: Contradictory arrival times across three documents
cases.rationale: Passenger has confirmed booking and boarded (S1.2 satisfied). Cause is carrier-controlled maintenance: APU replacement by WS line maintenance at LOS (S3.2(a)). Material contradiction: D3 and D4 differ on actual arrival time by over 3 hours — this determines whether the disruption qualifies under S2.1(b) (requires 3h30m+ delay). Per S8.3, when documents contradict on a material fact, request evidence naming the contradiction. Cannot assess compensation until this is resolved.

cases.title: Rejection citing weather contradicted by the operational record
cases.rationale: The flight cancellation qualifies as a carrier-controlled disruption under S3.2(b). Although the carrier claims extraordinary weather (S3.3(a)), the operational record (D3) directly contradicts this, showing the actual cause was crew duty time expiration following an HB-controlled rotation delay, with both airports reporting CAVOK weather. Per S3.6, the operational record governs. The passenger is entitled to 420 units (Band B for 2,750 km distance, 100% compensation under S4.2 since no re-routing alternative was offered). The rejection is validly challengeable under S9.1(a).

cases.title: Rejection that is correct and must not be challenged
cases.rationale: The flight was cancelled because Edinburgh Airport was closed to departures by the airport authority due to wind speeds exceeding safe limits during Storm Fionn. The operational record (D3) and airport authority bulletin (D4) both confirm this was an extraordinary circumstance under S3.3(a). Under S3.1, compensation is payable only for carrier-controlled causes. The carrier's rejection is valid and supported by the record.

cases.title: Angry passenger demanding premature escalation
cases.rationale: Flight cancelled due to carrier's IT systems failure (S3.2(c), D3). Notification sent 04 May 22:15 UTC, 10h45m before scheduled departure—less than 7 days notice triggers 100% compensation under S4.2. No re-routing exemption applies (D2: nothing further available). Distance 2,730 km is band B = 420 units (S5.1). Escalation to regulator is not yet permitted: S10.1(a) requires 56 days from filing; only 20 days elapsed. Claim is fully valid and meritorious; escalation becomes available at 56-day mark if carrier does not respond.

cases.title: Challenge ignored for thirty-five days, escalation ripe
cases.rationale: The operational record (D4) establishes this as a carrier-controlled technical fault under S3.2(a): engine oil filter contamination found by Altair's own maintenance at GRU, with no manufacturer directive. The carrier's rejection citing 'extraordinary technical circumstances' contradicts the record and is overridden by S3.6. The 7h 42m delay at final destination qualifies under S2.1(b); at Band C (7,930 km, 750 units), no reduction applies per S5.4 (5+ hours). The rejection is validly challengeable under S9.1(a). The passenger challenged on 18 Mar 2026; 35 days have now passed without response, satisfying S10.1(b) to escalate to the Synthetic Passenger Rights Body.

cases.title: Partial settlement: duty of care paid, compensation wrongly refused
cases.rationale: The flight qualifies under S2.1(a) (cancellation). Distance 2,900 km falls in band B; notification was given 2h35m before departure, triggering 100% compensation under S4.2 with no re-routing exemption. The carrier claims extraordinary weather, but the operational record (D3) explicitly states the cause was 'crew-rostering and dispatch platform outage...Internal'—an IT systems failure under S3.2(c). Per S3.6, the operational record governs. The carrier's rejection citing weather is validly challengeable under S9.1(a). Compensation due: 420 units. Duty of care of 300 units has been correctly reimbursed.

cases.title: Involuntary downgrade with no delay and no cancellation
cases.rationale: This is a pure involuntary downgrade with no cancellation or qualifying delay. S7.2 specifies that a downgrade is not a Part 5 compensation event and attracts only S7.1 reimbursement. The passenger paid 800 units for business class and is entitled to 40% of that fare: 320 units.

cases.title: Extraordinary cause with forty hours to recover
cases.rationale: Flight was cancelled, qualifying under S2.1(a). Although caused by a bird strike (extraordinary per S3.3(e)), 40 hours elapsed from the extraordinary event to scheduled departure, exceeding the 12-hour threshold in S3.5, so cause reverts to carrier-controlled. The carrier held two serviceable spare aircraft at HEL and did not assign either to IN300. Notice was 17.5 hours before departure (less than 7 days per S4.2: 100% compensation applies). Distance HEL-IST is 2,190 km, Band B per S5.1, yielding 420 units.

cases.title: Fleet-wide airworthiness directive, duty of care only
cases.rationale: The flight was cancelled (S2.1(a) qualifies), but the cause was an airworthiness directive for a latent manufacturing defect notified by the manufacturer and regulator (D3), which is extraordinary under S3.3(g). Since S3.1 restricts Part 5 compensation to carrier-controlled causes only, no compensation is payable despite Band C distance (5,555 km). However, duty of care is owed regardless of cause (S6.1): itemised receipts (D4) show 180 units in hotel and meal expenses, within the 300-unit cap (S6.3), and all evidence required by S8.1 is on file.

cases.title: Passenger overstates the delay; evidence shows just under threshold
cases.rationale: The claim is in scope: confirmed booking (D1), boarding pass evidence (D2), and filed within 18 months (flight 6 Apr 2026, now Aug 29 2026). However, it does not qualify under Part 2. The arrival record (D3) shows actual delay at final destination IST was 3 hours 20 minutes, but S2.1(b) requires 3 hours 30 minutes or more. The passenger falls 10 minutes short of the qualifying threshold. No cancellation (S2.1(a)) or denied boarding (S2.1(c)) occurred. Since no disruption under Part 2 qualifies, duty of care (S6.1) is not owed. The flight being carrier-controlled (crew delay per D4) is irrelevant without a qualifying disruption.

cases.title: Decisive fact buried at document eight of nine
cases.rationale: Flight GM212 was cancelled due to crew duty limit breach (S3.2(b), carrier-controlled). Notification sent 08 May at 13:20 for 12 May departure is 3 days 18 hours notice, less than 7 days. The carrier offered re-routing on GM216 departing 07:30 (30 minutes before original 08:00) and arriving 12:20 (1 hour 35 minutes after original 10:45). Both time windows satisfy S4.4 re-routing exemption for cancellations with less than 7 days notice, per D8. No Part 5 compensation is payable. Duty of care would require itemised receipts (S6.4), not provided or claimed.

cases.title: Two composed reductions at an exact band boundary
cases.rationale: Passenger arrived 3h 45m late at final destination (Amman), qualifying under S2.1(b). The inbound delay was caused by EM engineering hold at Amman (D4), a carrier-controlled maintenance fault under S3.2(a); the knock-on effect to EM604 is also carrier-controlled under S3.2(e). Distance is exactly 4,000 km per D1, placing the claim in Band B (420 units) under S5.3. Delay taper under S5.4 applies: 3h 45m falls within the 3h30m–5h bracket, reducing compensation to 50%. Final amount: 420 × 0.5 = 210 units.

cases.title: Rejection resting on a re-routing offer that is not in the record
cases.rationale: Passenger is entitled to full Band C compensation (750 units for 4,590 km distance per S5.1) for a carrier-controlled cancellation (commercial consolidation per S3.2(d)) notified less than 7 days in advance (S4.2). The carrier's rejection cites a re-routing exemption under S4.4, but the complete contact history (D4) shows no re-routing offer was ever made to the passenger. This is validly challengeable under S9.1(c): the operational record contradicts the carrier's stated ground.

cases.title: Strong claim filed nineteen months late
cases.rationale: The claim was filed on 12 Sep 2026, which is 19 months and 8 days after the scheduled departure of 04 Feb 2025 (D4). This exceeds the 18-month filing deadline set by S1.2(c). Per S1.3, a claim failing any limb of S1.2 is out of scope and receives no compensation or duty-of-care reimbursement.

cases.title: Receipts with a non-reimbursable item and a cap

derivation: S3.3(b) airspace closure by the air navigation service provider, not caused by the carrier -> extraordinary
S3.5 does not apply: the closure was still in force at the scheduled departure time
S6.1 duty of care is owed regardless of cause
S6.2(b) hotel 210.00 and airport transfer 21.00 are reimbursable
Replacement clothing is not among the categories in S6.2 and is not reimbursable, so 95.00 is excluded
S6.3 the cap is 300 units per passenger per disruption -> 300 units payable
S6.4 itemised receipts are present for every line

cases.title: Denied boarding, four hours late, no taper
cases.rationale: Passenger held confirmed booking, completed check-in at 06:11Z before 07:05 departure, and was involuntarily denied boarding due to overbooking (S2.1(c)), a carrier-controlled cause (S3.2(d)). Distance BRU–LIS is 1,720 km (band B, S5.1), yielding 420 units. Denied boarding is compensated at 100% without notice exemptions (S4.6). The passenger also qualifies under S2.1(b) by virtue of a 4h 20m delay to final destination; however, S5.4 taper (which would reduce to 50% for delays 3h30m–5h) applies only to claims qualifying under S2.1(b) *only*, so full compensation is due. No receipted duty-of-care claim presented. Carrier has not yet responded; claim is ready to submit.

cases.title: Stated cause contradicted by the record, where the policy resolves it
cases.rationale: Flight CV720 was cancelled due to crew sickness (first officer unfit, no standby available per D3), which is carrier-controlled under S3.2(b). The carrier falsely attributed the cancellation to ATC in D2, but S3.6 requires the operational record to govern; D3 and independent third-party record D4 confirm no ATC regulation affected this flight. Passenger meets all S1.2 criteria: confirmed booking (D1), checked in (D8), within 18-month filing window. Notification at 04:50 UTC for 06:40 departure is ~2 hours (less than 7 days per S4.2), yielding 100% compensation; no specific re-routing offer is documented (S4.4 does not apply). Distance 1,450 km places booking in Band B (S5.1): 420 units. No duty-of-care expenses claimed (D6). Evidence sufficient under S8.1.

cases.title: Settlement offer that matches the full entitlement
cases.rationale: The claim is in scope and qualifies under S2.1(a) as VT640 was cancelled. The cause is carrier-controlled per S3.2(c) (VT's IT system failure, per D3 operational record). Compensation is 420 units under Band B (S5.1: 1,600 km distance from D1), payable in full because notice was 2h 25m (less than 7 days per S4.2) and the offered re-routing on 07 Dec does not qualify for S4.4 exemption (more than 1 hour before original). Duty of care is 170 units, fully supported by itemised receipts (D4) and within the 300-unit cap (S6.2, S6.3). The settlement of 590 units exactly meets full entitlement; per S9.4 it should be accepted.
